L00001: # TableBench L00002:
L00003: L00004: L00005: L00006: L00007: L00008: L00009:
L00010: L00011: Official repository for paper `TableBench: A Comprehensive and Complex Benchmark for Table Question Answering` L00012: L00013:

L00014: 📚 Paper L00015:    L00016: 🏆 Leaderboard L00017:    L00018: 🤗 TableBench L00019:    L00020: 🤗 TableInstruct L00021:

L00022: L00023: ## News L00024: > **🔥Apr. 18, 2025🔥** L00025: > L00026: > 1. **☀️ Enhanced TableBench**: L00027: > We’ve released an cleaner version of TableBench, after thoroughly reviewing all test set cases and correcting any errors we identified. Please download the latest version of [TableBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Multilingual-Multimodal-NLP/TableBench) for the most accurate dataset. L00028: > L00029: > 2. **🚀 Brand New Leaderboard**: L00030: > The brand new [Leaderboard](https://tablebench.github.io/) is now live! We've included the performance of many newly released models in our latest leaderboard and will continue to keep it up to date. Submissions are welcome! For submission guidelines, please refer to the `Submission section` on [Leaderboard](https://tablebench.github.io/) website. L00031: > L00032: > 3. **🔍 Refined Evaluation Metrics**: L00033: > In response to community feedback and in-depth discussions, we've updated the evaluation metrics for Fact Checking, Numerical Reasoning, and Data Analysis. You can find the detailed specifications of these new metrics in Section `📐 Evaluation Metrics` L00034: > L00035: > **🚀Jan. 21, 2025🚀**: L00036: > L00037: > We are thrilled to share that our paper has been accepted to AAAI 2025! We sincerely thank our co-authors, the anonymous reviewers, and all the researchers and users on GitHub or through email whose valuable feedback and support have greatly contributed to this work. L00038: L00039: ## 🧾 Overview L00040: TableBench is a comprehensive and complex L00041: benchmark designed to evaluate Table L00042: Question Answering (TableQA) capabilities, aligning closely with the "Reasoning Complexity of L00043: Questions" dimension in real-world Table QA scenarios. It covers 18 question L00044: categories L00045: across 4 major ategories—including Fact Checking, Numerical Reasoning, Data L00046: Analysis, and Visualization—with 886 carefully curated test cases. TableBench L00047: substantially pushes the boundaries of large language models in complex TableQA scenarios. L00048:

L00049: L00050:

L00051: L00052: ## 📐 Evaluation Metrics L00053: L00054: This module defines evaluation metrics for various sub-tasks: L00055: L00056: ### 🔍 Fact Checking L00057: - **Metric:** Exact Match (EM) L00058: - **Description:** Assesses whether the predicted statement exactly matches the reference. L00059: L00060: ### 🔢 Numerical Reasoning L00061: - **Metric:** Exact Match (EM) L00062: - **Description:** Focuses on the correctness of numerical outputs. L00063: L00064: ### 📈 Data Analysis L00065: - Metrics vary based on sub-task type: L00066: L00067: | Task Type | Metric | Description | L00068: |------------------------|-------------------|------------------------------------------------------------| L00069: | Impact Analysis | Exact Match (EM) | Requires precise match of influential factors | L00070: | Correlation Analysis | EM_with_error_10 | Allows ±10% numerical margin of error | L00071: | Trend Forecasting | EM_with_error_10 | Allows ±10% numerical margin of error | L00072: | Statistical Analysis | EM_with_error_10 | Allows ±10% numerical margin of error | L00073: | Other Data Analysis Tasks | ROUGE-L | Suitable for open-ended, textual responses | L00074: L00075: ### 📊 Visualization L00076: - **Metric:** Pass@1 L00077: - **Description:** Measures whether the correct chart is generated on the first attempt. L00078: L00079: --- L00080: L00081: ## 🔧 How to evaluate on Tablebench L00082: L00083: ### Step 1. Download the Dataset L00084: L00085: Download the latest version of [**TableBench**](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Multilingual-Multimodal-NLP/TableBench) from Hugging Face and place it in your working directory. L00086: L00087: ### Step 2. Run Inference with Your LLM L00088: L00089: Use your preferred Large Language Model (LLM) to generate predictions for each test case. L00090: L00091: Important notes: L00092: - Store your model's predictions in the `prediction` field L00093: - Include your model name in the `model_name` field L00094: L00095: Example JSON structure: L00096: ```json L00097: [ L00098: { L00099: ... L00100: "model_name": "your-model-name-here", L00101: "prediction": "Final Answer: 1062" L00102: }, L00103: ... L00104: ] L00105: ``` L00106: We provide an example inference result file at: `eval_examples/inference_results/o3-mini-2025-01-31=TableBench_DP=Example.jsonl` L00107: L00108: L00109: ### Step 3. Parse Final Answers from LLM Predictions L00110: Use our parsing script to extract final answers from your model's predictions. The script `parse_tablebench_instruction_response_script.py` includes a main method example: L00111: L00112: ```python L00113: if __name__ == '__main__': L00114: # ==== Global settings ==== L00115: PROJECT_ROOT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) L00116: EXP_DIR = 'eval_examples' L00117: L00118: INFERENCE_RESULT_DIR = f'{PROJECT_ROOT_DIR}/{EXP_DIR}/inference_results' L00119: PARSED_RUSULT_DIR = f'{PROJECT_ROOT_DIR}/{EXP_DIR}/parsed_results' L00120: L00121: # ==== Load inference results ==== L00122: for inference_result_file in iter_file_from_dir(f'{INFERENCE_RESULT_DIR}', '.jsonl'): L00123: print(f'Parsing {inference_result_file}') L00124: # === Load inference results === L00125: inference_results = read_json_file(inference_result_file) L00126: if not isinstance(inference_results, list): L00127: inference_results = [inference_results] L00128: # === Parse inference results === L00129: parsed_results = parse_inference_results(inference_results) L00130: # === Save parsed results === L00131: write_json_to_file( L00132: f'{PARSED_RUSULT_DIR}/{os.path.basename(inference_result_file)}', parsed_results, is_json_line=True) L00133: print('Parsing completed.') L00134: ``` L00135: L00136: ### Step 4. Evaluate the Results L00137: After parsing the predictions, use our evaluation script to assess your model's performance. L00138: A main function example is provided in `eval_tablebench_script.py` L00139: L00140: ```python L00141: if __name__ == '__main__': L00142: L00143: # ==== Global settings ==== L00144: PROJECT_ROOT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) L00145: EXP_DIR = 'eval_examples' L00146: L00147: PARSED_RUSULT_DIR = f'{PROJECT_ROOT_DIR}/{EXP_DIR}/parsed_results' L00148: EVAL_RESULT_DIR = f'{PROJECT_ROOT_DIR}/{EXP_DIR}/evaluation_results' L00149: L00150: # Init metric evaluation engine L00151: metric_eval_engine = QAMetric() L00152: L00153: # Merge parsed results to one file L00154: overall_sim_inference_results_path = merge_parsed_results_to_one_sim_file( L00155: PARSED_RUSULT_DIR, EVAL_RESULT_DIR) L00156: L00157: # Support add multiple inference result files L00158: candidate_eval_file_paths = [ L00159: overall_sim_inference_results_path L00160: ] L00161: L00162: # Support eval targeted models,if eval_models is empty, all models will be eval L00163: eval_models = [ L00164: # 'o3-mini-2025-01-31', L00165: ] L00166: L00167: # Load the candidate evaluation results L00168: categoried_llm_inference_results = build_categoried_llm_inference_results( L00169: candidate_eval_file_paths, eval_models) L00170: L00171: # Evaluate by subtype L00172: print('==== Evaluate by subtype ====') L00173: llm_eval_subtype_results = eval_by_subtype( L00174: categoried_llm_inference_results, metric_eval_engine) L00175: # sve_subtype_results to csv L00176: llm_eval_subtype_results_csv_path = f'{EVAL_RESULT_DIR}/llm_eval_subtype_results.csv' L00177: save_subtype_results_to_csv( L00178: llm_eval_subtype_results, llm_eval_subtype_results_csv_path) L00179: L00180: # Evaluate by type L00181: print('==== Evaluate by type ====') L00182: llm_eval_type_results = eval_by_type( L00183: categoried_llm_inference_results, metric_eval_engine) L00184: # save_type_results to csv L00185: llm_eval_type_results_csv_path = f'{EVAL_RESULT_DIR}/llm_eval_type_results.csv' L00186: save_type_results_to_csv( L00187: llm_eval_type_results, llm_eval_type_results_csv_path) L00188: ``` L00189: L00190: The final evaluation results will be stored in `eval_examples/evaluation_results`, including both `json` and `csv` formats. L00191: L00192: ### Terminology L00193: `parse@1`: Indicates whether the final answer was successfully parsed in a single run. This is a boolean value used to assess the LLM's ability to follow the expected output format. L00194: L00195: `ecr@1`: Stands for "execution correctness rate at 1". It checks whether the Python code generated by the LLM can run without errors on the first attempt. This metric reflects the correctness of code generation. L00196: L00197: `pass@1`: Used for the `chart_generation` task, this indicates whether the generated result passes the provided test cases in a single attempt. L00001: from utils.file_util import read_json_file, write_json_to_file, iter_file_from_dir
L00002: from metrics.qa_metrics import QAMetric
L00003: import pandas as pd
L00004: import os
L00005: 
L00006: """
L00007: Evaluation Metric Instruction
L00008: 
L00009: This module defines the evaluation metrics used for different types of tasks in the system:
L00010: 
L00011: - Fact Checking:
L00012:   Uses Exact Match (EM) as the evaluation metric to assess whether the predicted statement exactly matches the reference.
L00013: 
L00014: - Numerical Reasoning:
L00015:   Also evaluated using Exact Match (EM), focusing on the correctness of numerical outputs.
L00016: 
L00017: - Data Analysis:
L00018:   Subdivided into specific categories with tailored metrics:
L00019:     - Correlation Analysis, Trend Forecasting, and Statistical Analysis:
L00020:       Evaluated using EM_with_error_10, allowing a 10% margin of error in numerical predictions.
L00021:     - Impact Analysis:
L00022:       Assessed with strict Exact Match (EM) to ensure precise identification of influential factors.
L00023:     - Others:
L00024:       Evaluated using ROUGE-L, suitable for more open-ended or textual responses in data-related tasks.
L00025: 
L00026: - Visualization:
L00027:   Assessed using Pass@1, which measures the success rate of producing a correct result in the first attempt.
L00028: 
L00029: These metric assignments help ensure fair and task-appropriate evaluation across various capabilities.
L00030: """
L00031: 
L00032: 
L00033: def merge_parsed_results_to_one_sim_file(parsed_results_dir, eval_results_dir):
L00034:     overall_sim_inference_results_path = f'{eval_results_dir}/overall_sim_inference_results.json'
L00035:     overall_results = []
L00036:     for file_path in iter_file_from_dir(parsed_results_dir):
L00037:         exp_results = read_json_file(file_path)
L00038:         if not isinstance(exp_results, list):
L00039:             exp_results = [exp_results]
L00040:         for result in exp_results:
L00041:             result.pop('instruction')
L00042:             result.pop('prediction')
L00043:             overall_results.append(result)
L00044:     write_json_to_file(
L00045:         overall_sim_inference_results_path, overall_results)
L00046:     print(
L00047:         f'Save overall results to {overall_sim_inference_results_path}')
L00048:     return overall_sim_inference_results_path
L00049: 
L00050: 
L00051: def build_categoried_llm_inference_results(candidate_eval_file_paths, eval_models):
L00052:     """
L00053:     The `categoried_llm_inference_results` structure is formatted as follows:
L00054: 
L00055:     {
L00056:         "model_name/instruction_type": {
L00057:             "merged_type_1": [result_1, result_2, ...],
L00058:             "merged_type_2": [result_1, result_2, ...],
L00059:             ...
L00060:         }
L00061:     }
L00062: 
L00063:     - The top-level key combines the model name and instruction type, typically separated by a slash (e.g., "GPT-4/DP").
L00064:     - Each value is a dictionary that maps a merged task type (e.g., "FactChecking_NumericalReasoning_Aggregation", "FactChecking_MatchBased") to a list of inference results.
L00065:     - Each result in the list represents the model's output on an individual instance of that task type.
L00066: 
L00067:     This structure is used to organize and analyze inference results by model configuration and task category.
L00068:     """
L00069:     candidate_eval_results = []
L00070:     for file_path in candidate_eval_file_paths:
L00071:         data = read_json_file(file_path)
L00072:         candidate_eval_results.extend(data)
L00073:     categoried_llm_inference_results = {}
L00074:     for result in candidate_eval_results:
L00075:         model_name = result['model_name']
L00076:         if len(eval_models) != 0 and model_name not in eval_models:
L00077:             continue
L00078:         type = result['qtype']
L00079:         subtype = result['qsubtype']
L00080:         merged_type = f'{type}_{subtype}'
L00081:         instruction_type = result['instruction_type']
L00082:         llm_reasoning_method = f'{model_name}/{instruction_type}'
L00083:         if llm_reasoning_method not in categoried_llm_inference_results:
L00084:             categoried_llm_inference_results[llm_reasoning_method] = {}
L00085:         if merged_type not in categoried_llm_inference_results[llm_reasoning_method]:
L00086:             categoried_llm_inference_results[llm_reasoning_method][merged_type] = [
L00087:             ]
L00088:         categoried_llm_inference_results[llm_reasoning_method][merged_type].append(
L00089:             result)
L00090:     return categoried_llm_inference_results
L00091: 
L00092: 
L00093: def eval_by_subtype(categoried_llm_inference_results, metric_eval_engine):
L00094:     """
L00095:     The `llm_eval_subtype_results` structure is formatted as follows:
L00096: 
L00097:     {
L00098:         "model_name/instruction_type": {
L00099:             "merged_type_1": {
L00100:                 "metric_1": score,
L00101:                 "metric_2": score,
L00102:                 ...
L00103:             },
L00104:             "merged_type_2": {
L00105:                 "metric_1": score,
L00106:                 "metric_2": score,
L00107:                 ...
L00108:             },
L00109:             ...
L00110:         }
L00111:     }
L00112: 
L00113:     Description:
L00114:     - The top-level key is a string combining the model name and instruction type (e.g., "GPT-4/DP").
L00115:     - Each value is a dictionary mapping a merged task type (e.g., "FactChecking_NumericalReasoning_Aggregation", "FactChecking_MatchBased") to its evaluation results.
L00116:     - For each task type, metrics (e.g., "EM", "ROUGE-L", "Pass@1") are mapped to their corresponding evaluation scores (usually floats).
L00117:     """
L00118: 
L00119:     llm_eval_subtype_results_path = f'{EVAL_RESULT_DIR}/llm_eval_subtype_results.json'
L00120:     llm_eval_subtype_results = {}
L00121:     # evlaute by subtype
L00122:     for llm_reasoning_method, result in categoried_llm_inference_results.items():
L00123:         print(f'Processing {llm_reasoning_method}...')
L00124:         for merged_type, results in result.items():
L00125:             # Calculate the metric on visualization
L00126:             if merged_type == 'Visualization_ChartGeneration':
L00127:                 metric_scores = {
L00128:                 }
L00129:                 total = len(results)
L00130:                 metric_scores['total'] = total
L00131:                 # Code Excution Result
L00132:                 ecr_1_acc = None
L00133:                 ecr_1s = [result["parsed_result"].get('ecr_1', None)
L00134:                           for result in results]
L00135:                 ecr_1_acc = ecr_1s.count(True) / total
L00136:                 metric_scores['ECR@1'] = round(ecr_1_acc*100, 2)
L00137:                 # Code Pass@1 Result
L00138:                 pass_1_acc = None
L00139:                 pass_1s = [result["parsed_result"].get('parsed_prediction', None)
L00140:                            for result in results]
L00141:                 pass_1_acc = pass_1s.count(True) / total
L00142:                 metric_scores['Pass@1'] = round(pass_1_acc * 100, 2)
L00143:             else:
L00144:                 predictions = [result["parsed_result"]
L00145:                                ['parsed_prediction'] for result in results]
L00146:                 references = [result['answer'] for result in results]
L00147:                 metric_scores = metric_eval_engine.compute(
L00148:                     references=references, predictions=predictions)
L00149:                 total = len(predictions)
L00150:                 metric_scores['total'] = total
L00151:                 if llm_reasoning_method.split('/')[1] == 'PoT':
L00152:                     ecr_1_acc = None
L00153:                     ecr_1s = [result["parsed_result"].get('ecr_1', None)
L00154:                               for result in results]
L00155:                     ecr_1_acc = ecr_1s.count(True) / total
L00156:                     metric_scores['ECR@1'] = round(ecr_1_acc*100, 2)
L00157:             # Calculate the ratio of successfully parsed results
L00158:             parse_1s = [result["parsed_result"].get(
L00159:                 'Parse@1', None) for result in results]
L00160:             metric_scores['Parse@1'] = round(
L00161:                 parse_1s.count(True) / total * 100, 2)
L00162:             if llm_reasoning_method not in llm_eval_subtype_results:
L00163:                 llm_eval_subtype_results[llm_reasoning_method] = {}
L00164:             llm_eval_subtype_results[llm_reasoning_method][merged_type] = metric_scores
L00165:     write_json_to_file(llm_eval_subtype_results_path, llm_eval_subtype_results)
L00166: 
L00167:     return llm_eval_subtype_results
L00168: 
L00169: 
L00170: def eval_by_type(categoried_llm_inference_results, metric_eval_engine):
L00171:     """
L00172:     The `llm_eval_type_results` structure is formatted as follows::
L00173: 
L00174:     {
L00175:         "model_name/instruction_type": {
L00176:             "FactChecking": {
L00177:                 "metric_1": score,
L00178:                 "metric_2": score,
L00179:                 ...
L00180:             },
L00181:             "NumericalReasoning": {
L00182:                 "metric_1": score,
L00183:                 "metric_2": score,
L00184:                 ...
L00185:             },
L00186:             "DataAnalysis": {
L00187:                 "metric_1": score,
L00188:                 "metric_2": score,
L00189:                 ...
L00190:             },
L00191:             "Visualization": {
L00192:                 "metric_1": score,
L00193:                 "metric_2": score,
L00194:                 ...
L00195:             },
L00196:             "Overall": {
L00197:                 "metric_1": score,
L00198:                 "metric_2": score,
L00199:                 ...
L00200:             }
L00201:         }
L00202:     }
L00203: 
L00204:     Description:
L00205:     - The top-level key is a string combining the model name and instruction type (e.g., "GPT4/DP").
L00206:     - Each value is a dictionary mapping an individual task type (e.g., "FactChecking", "DataAnalysis") to its evaluation results.
L00207:     - For each task type, the dictionary contains metric names (such as "EM", "ROUGE-L", "Pass@1") mapped to their respective scores (typically floats).
L00208: 
L00209:     This structure provides a fine-grained view of evaluation scores per task type for each model and instruction configuration.
L00210:     """
L00211:     llm_eval_type_results_path = f'{EVAL_RESULT_DIR}/llm_eval_type_results.json'
L00212:     llm_eval_type_results = {}
L00213:     # evlaute by subtype
L00214:     for llm_reasoning_method, result in categoried_llm_inference_results.items():
L00215:         llm_eval_type_result = {}
L00216:         qtype_dict = {}
L00217:         print(f'Processing {llm_reasoning_method}...')
L00218:         # categoried single exp results by qtype
L00219:         for merged_type, results in result.items():
L00220:             qtype = merged_type.split('_')[0]
L00221:             if qtype not in qtype_dict:
L00222:                 qtype_dict[qtype] = []
L00223:             qtype_dict[qtype].extend(results)
L00224:         # calculate the metric for each qtype
L00225:         # == FactChecking ==
L00226:         fc_results = qtype_dict['FactChecking']
L00227:         fc_predictions = [fc_result["parsed_result"]
L00228:                           ['parsed_prediction'] for fc_result in fc_results]
L00229:         fc_references = [fc_result['answer'] for fc_result in fc_results]
L00230:         fc_metric_scores = metric_eval_engine.compute(
L00231:             references=fc_references, predictions=fc_predictions)
L00232:         # Calculate the ratio of successfully parsed results
L00233:         fc_parse_1s = [fc_result["parsed_result"].get(
L00234:             'Parse@1', None) for fc_result in fc_results]
L00235:         fc_metric_scores['Parse@1'] = round(
L00236:             fc_parse_1s.count(True) / len(fc_results) * 100, 2)
L00237:         fc_metric_scores['total'] = len(fc_results)
L00238:         # In Case Instruction type is PoT
L00239:         if llm_reasoning_method.split('/')[1] == 'PoT':
L00240:             # Calculate the ratio of successfully excution results
L00241:             fc_ecr_1s = [fc_result["parsed_result"].get(
L00242:                 'ecr_1', None) for fc_result in fc_results]
L00243:             fc_metric_scores['ECR@1'] = round(
L00244:                 fc_ecr_1s.count(True) / len(fc_results) * 100, 2)
L00245:         llm_eval_type_result['FactChecking'] = fc_metric_scores
L00246: 
L00247:         # == NumericalReasoning ==
L00248:         nr_results = qtype_dict['NumericalReasoning']
L00249:         nr_predictions = [nr_result["parsed_result"]
L00250:                           ['parsed_prediction'] for nr_result in nr_results]
L00251:         nr_references = [nr_result['answer'] for nr_result in nr_results]
L00252:         nr_metric_scores = metric_eval_engine.compute(
L00253:             references=nr_references, predictions=nr_predictions)
L00254:         # Calculate the ratio of successfully parsed results
L00255:         nr_parse_1s = [nr_result["parsed_result"].get(
L00256:             'Parse@1', None) for nr_result in nr_results]
L00257:         nr_metric_scores['Parse@1'] = round(
L00258:             nr_parse_1s.count(True) / len(nr_results) * 100, 2)
L00259:         nr_metric_scores['total'] = len(nr_results)
L00260:         # In Case Instruction type is PoT
L00261:         if llm_reasoning_method.split('/')[1] == 'PoT':
L00262:             # Calculate the ratio of successfully excution results
L00263:             nr_ecr_1s = [nr_result["parsed_result"].get(
L00264:                 'ecr_1', None) for nr_result in nr_results]
L00265:             nr_metric_scores['ECR@1'] = round(
L00266:                 nr_ecr_1s.count(True) / len(nr_results) * 100, 2)
L00267:

L00001: from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
L00002: 
L00003: class BaseMetric(ABC):
L00004: 
L00005:     @abstractmethod
L00006:     def __init__(self, **kwargs):
L00007:         pass
L00008: 
L00009:     @abstractmethod
L00010:     def compute(self,references,predictions):
L00011:         pass
L00012:
